spots.name: Kingdom Centre

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Kingdom Centre, formerly Kingdom Tower, is a 99-story, 302.3 m (992 ft) skyscraper in the al-Olaya district of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. When completed in 2002, it overtook the 267-meter (876 ft) Faisaliah Tower as the tallest tower in Saudi Arabia.

spots.name: Al Yamamah Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Al Yamamah Palace is the official workplace and residence of the King of Saudi Arabia and the seat of the royal court since 1988. Named after the historic al-Yamama region, the palace is located in the al-Hada district of northwestern Riyadh and was built in 1988 during the reign of King Fahd bin Abdulaziz.

spots.name: Deera Square
spots.summary: Deera Square, also known as Justice Square, Safa Square or derisively as Chop-Chop Square, is a public space in the Ad-Dirah neighborhood of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. It is located adjacent to the al-Hukm Palace compound and Imam Turki bin Abdullah Grand Mosque in the Qasr al-Hukm District.

spots.name: Masmak Fort

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Al Masmak Palace, also called the Masmak Fortress or Masmak Fort, is a historic clay and mudbrick fort in the ad-Dirah neighborhood of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, located in close proximity to the al-Hukm Palace in the Qasr al-Hukm District.

spots.name: Al Faisaliah Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Al-Faisaliah Tower is a 267-metre-high commercial skyscraper and mixed-use complex located in the Al-Olaya district of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Designed by Foster + Partners, the tower is the centerpiece of the Al-Faisaliah Center development.

spots.name: Al Oud cemetery
spots.summary: Al Oud Cemetery is a public cemetery in the al-Owd neighbourhood of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, known for being the resting place of several members of the Saudi royal family. The word "al-ʿŪud", in Peninsular Arabic means "elder ", likely referring to King Abdulaziz, who was buried in the cemetery.

spots.name: King Salman Park
spots.summary: King Salman Park, one of Riyadh’s mega-projects, is an urban area being developed in the city of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia under the supervision of the King Salman Park Foundation. It was unveiled in 2019 as part of the Green Riyadh initiative aimed at increasing the green space of Riyadh.

spots.name: Murabba Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Murabba Palace is a historic palace in the al-Murabba neighborhood of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, located in the King Abdulaziz Historical Center.

spots.name: Riyadh Water Tower
spots.summary: Riyadh Water Tower, locally known as Burj al-Khazzaan or simply al-Khazzaan, is a 61-meters tall conical-shaped cylindrical water tower and a prominent cultural landmark in the al-Futah neighborhood of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

spots.name: Imam Turki bin Abdullah Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Imam Turki bin Abdullah Grand Mosque, also known as the Grand Mosque of Riyadh, is a Sunni Islam Friday mosque in the ad-Dirah neighborhood of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, located adjacent to al-Hukm Palace compound, in Deera Square.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Imam Turki bin Abdullah Grand Mosque

spots.name: King Abdullah Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The King Abdullah Mosque, formerly Prince Abdullah Mosque and officially as the Mosque of King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, is a mosque in the al-Olaya district of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, located on the 77th floor of the Kingdom Centre.

spots.name: King Abdulaziz Historical Center

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sun

spots.summary: King Abdulaziz Historical Center (KAHC) (Arabic: مركز الملك عبدالعزيز التاريخي) is a cross-district heritage complex in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, covering south of al-Murabba and north of al-Futah.

spots.name: Riyadh TV Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Riyadh TV Tower is a 170-metre-high (560 ft) television tower in the Al-Wisham neighborhood of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Construction began in 1975 and was completed in 1982. It was the tallest structure in Saudi Arabia from 1982 until 2000, when it was surpassed by Al-Faisaliah Tower.

spots.name: King Khalid Grand Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The King Khalid Grand Mosque is a Sunni Islam Friday mosque and an active place of worship in the Umm al-Hammam al-Gharbi neighborhood of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Built in 1987 and opened in 1988, it incorporates some elements of Turkish architecture and is one of the most prominent landmarks of Riyadh.

spots.name: King Fahad National Library

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The King Fahad National Library is the legal deposit and copyright library for Saudi Arabia. The project was announced in 1983 in response to an initiative made by the people of Riyadh when King Fahd ascended the throne, and the implementation started in 1986. The library opened in Riyadh in 1990.

spots.name: Salam Park
spots.summary: Salam Park is a 61-acre historic urban park in the al-Salam district of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, located southwest of Qasr al-Hukm District. Opened in 2004, it was built on the site of an eponymous date palm orchard that belonged to Prince Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman.

spots.name: Qaṣr al-Shamsīyya

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Qaṣr al-Shamsīyya is a ruined palace in the al-Futah district of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. It was built for Princess Nura bint ʿAbd al-Raḥman (1875–1950), the elder sister of King ʾAbd al-ʿAzīz Ibn Saud. The palace was north of the old town, not far from the Murabba Palace.

spots.name: Al-Qibli Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Al-Qibli Mosque is a historic mosque in the Manfuhah neighborhood of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The origins of the mosque have been traced as far back as 1689 and is one of the oldest mosques in Riyadh.

spots.name: Al Hugayet Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Al Hugayet Tower is a tower in Khobar, Saudi Arabia. The tower was completed in 2011. It is 140 metres tall and has 26 floors.

spots.name: Prince Faisal bin Fahd Sports City
spots.summary: Prince Faisal bin Fahd Sports City Stadium is a multi-purpose stadium in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. It is set to be a venue for the 2034 FIFA World Cup and has a proposed capacity of 46,865 people following refurbishments, where it will host fixtures in the group stage and round of 32.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Prince Faisal bin Fahd Sports City Stadium

spots.name: Al-Faisal Museum for Arab-Islamic Art

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Al-Faisal Museum for Arab-Islamic Art is an art museum in the al-Olaya district of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, located next to the Al Faisaliah Tower in the building of King Faisal Center for Research and Islamic Studies.
